Pre-Production Canon Cleanup Addendum
LOCKED v1.0 • 27 August 2026
STATUS — COMPLETE / LOCKED

This project-wide addendum records the final pre-repository cleanup rulings approved after the 17-checklist audit. It exists to remove ambiguity while the older source files are consolidated into clean active versions for Git. It does not reopen unrelated mechanics.
1. Reserve access — Aeric in every town

Chaplain Aeric Solm is the single canonical reserve caretaker and move relearner, and he appears in every town. Therefore every town provides reserve and free move-relearner access through Aeric himself.
• Aeric is the sole normal NPC who opens the reserve-management interface.
• Aeric is the sole normal NPC who provides the free move-relearner service.
• Every town contains an authored Aeric service position/interaction.
• This is the same recurring character, not a different local storage NPC or local caretaker.
• Alchemists heal the active travelling party only and never open reserve management.
• There is no pause-menu or field-based remote reserve withdrawal.
• A full-party capture may still deposit a captured Abyssal into reserve automatically; this remains one-way field deposit, not remote access.
• Hostile routes, caves, dungeons and battles do not gain reserve withdrawal merely because Aeric is present in every town.
2. Documents affected by the Aeric ruling

rows: Replace the statement that the shared reserve can be represented by different local NPCs/facilities. Every town's reserve service is specifically Aeric.
Section 9's Aeric-only rule remains. The previously deferred location question is now closed: Aeric is physically available in every town.
Its Aeric-only service contract remains. Add explicit every-town placement for Aeric's RESERVE / RELEARN MOVES / LEAVE interaction.
Free Aeric relearning remains unchanged; every town now supplies a legal Aeric access point.

blocks.text: 3. Checklist 17 verification

Checklist 17 — Overworld Interaction Rules v1.0 has been located and verified as COMPLETE & LOCKED. Its 16×16 logical grid, four-direction movement, fixed screen-to-screen presentation, explicit collision/warps, trainer line-of-sight, step-based wild encounters, Skiff traversal, persistent object IDs, Objectives menu, town restoration state swaps, mutual-final-KO Aeric recovery and soft-lock safety rules remain active.
The only cleanup amendment required by the present pass is the explicit statement that Aeric is available in every town.
4. Human restoration conflict
Resolved by Checklist 09 v1.2 correction: five total human restorations, all elective. Pate and Trade are optional targets, not automatic uses.
5. Execution-proxy conflict
Resolved: eighteen generic primary-Type proxies, one for every canonical type. Checklist 09 v1.0's twelve-proxy wording is superseded.
6. Checklist 01 authority

A standalone Checklist 01 — Exact Stat Growth Algorithm LOCKED v1.0 has now been consolidated from the validated growth/evolution workbook and existing dependent checklist references. It becomes the readable implementation authority alongside the canonical workbook.
7. Encounter tables — only substantive unfinished pre-production content

The encounter framework is locked, but the route/habitat species tables are not yet fully authored. The next closure task is to create DAY and NIGHT encounter tables for every encounter-enabled route/habitat, with authored level ranges and weights totaling exactly 100%.
• Wild levels remain authored and never dynamically scale to the player's party.
• Each encounter-enabled habitat has separate DAY and NIGHT tables.
• The world alternates every 10 real-time minutes; Hell uses the same mechanical cycle as Pale/Dark phases.
• Encounter density uses the locked LOW / NORMAL / HIGH model unless an authored zone value overrides it.
• The Resonator suppresses generated encounters at least 5 levels below the first living party Abyssal; it never rerolls repeatedly for a stronger result.
• Story-choice opposite evolutions remain subject to Checklist 11's postgame Primeval Reach access rule.
8. Reference/version cleanup rule
• Checklist 09 v1.0 is superseded and must be archived as historical only.
• Checklist 09 v1.1 is superseded as the standalone active version by the v1.2 correction authority; its eighteen-proxy content is retained.
• When the final repository source pack is regenerated, Checklist 13 and Checklist 15 references to Checklist 09 v1.0 must be replaced with Checklist 09 v1.2.
• Checklist 16 references to Checklist 09 v1.1 must be replaced with Checklist 09 v1.2.
• Checklist 15's note describing the Pate/Trade discrepancy may be removed or marked RESOLVED.
• Checklist 02/03's generic alternate-local-reserve-provider wording must be removed.
• Checklist 08/17 must explicitly encode Aeric's every-town availability.
• The final repo will include one Canon Source Index identifying exactly one active authority chain and separating superseded files from active files.
